ios.desc:
Zone: Stay Focused, Block Distractions, Take Back Your Time

Zone is the focus app that helps you stay focused, block apps and websites, and build deep work habits. With app lock controls, scheduled blocking, a focus timer, and screen time insights, Zone turns your phone from a distraction into your productivity partner. Refocus your mind, track hours, and get more done every single day.

Block Apps and Websites Instantly  
Choose distracting apps and lock them when you start a Zone. Social media, games, shopping, anything that pulls your attention can be blocked with one tap. When apps are blocked, your screen becomes a minimalist phone designed to help you move forward, not fall into scrolling loops.

Focus Timer to Lock In  
Start a focus session and go into deep work mode. Time spent focused is tracked automatically. You can see how long you stayed on task, compare with screen time, and build streaks. Every Zone helps you develop stronger attention, flow, and discipline.

Schedule App Blocking  
Create routines for mornings, work hours, study time, or sleep. App blocking turns on at the right times automatically so you do not rely on willpower. Keep nights free from screens, improve sleep, and automate productivity habits.

Time and Screen Insights  
Zone gives you more than just a screen time number. It helps you understand how many minutes you won back by staying off distracting apps. Compare your focused hours to last week, find your best days, and see your progress clearly.

Make Your Own Zones  
Study Zone, Work Zone, Gym Zone, Reading Zone, Meditation Zone, Sleep Zone. You pick the purpose, you pick what gets blocked. Hit Start Focus and get into the state of attention you want. Build a system around your goals, not around apps.

Minimalist and Easy to Use  
Zone is designed for clarity. No noise, no complex settings, no unnecessary notifications. Just start a focus session and distractions disappear. The goal is to be present in real life, not inside your phone.

Perfect for Anyone Wanting Control  
If you face procrastination, digital addiction, doomscrolling, ADHD focus struggles, or just want more time for yourself, Zone gives you structure that works. It is an ADHD planner mixed with a powerful app blocker and straightforward time tracker.

Screen Time Control Done Right

App lock to stop impulsive opens  
Block apps and websites while focusing  
Hide apps so your phone becomes a dumb phone  
Focus timer that supports deep work  
Track hours

quotes.text:
I built Zone, an iOS app blocker using Apple's Family Controls API. The differentiator is simple: it counts how many times you try to open blocked apps.
Most app blockers just block. But I found the attempt count more revealing than the block itself. Seeing "you tried to open Instagram 47 times today" was a wake-up call I didn't get from blocking alone.
Technical notes: Family Controls API is poorly documented but provides system-level blocking that actually works (unlike overlay approaches). Had to handle some edge cases around authorization persistence and count tracking across app restarts. The API requires Screen Time permissions which adds friction to onboarding but ensures reliable blocking.
One interesting discovery: users seem to prefer seeing raw attempt counts over gamified metrics (streaks, badges, etc). Less is more for this use case.
Built in SwiftUI, local storage only, no subscriptions. Took about 3 months part-time.
Curious if others have worked with Family Controls API and what challenges you faced. Also interested in thoughts on digital wellness apps in general - does tracking behavior change it, or just make you more aware without actual change?

quotes.text:
Hey HN! I built Zone, an iOS app blocker with usage attempt tracking.
The core idea: most app blockers just block apps, but I wanted to see how often I was actually trying to open them. Turns out I was attempting to open Instagram 40+ times a day without even realizing it. That number was more effective at changing behavior than just blocking alone.
Technical bits:

Built using Apple's Family Controls API (which was... interesting to work with)
Tracks block attempts without storing any actual usage data
Simple scheduling system for focus sessions
No subscription model - one-time unlock

The Family Controls API is pretty powerful but has some quirks - you need to use Screen Time authorization, and the blocking is system-level so it's actually reliable (unlike overlays or redirects).
Started this as a personal tool after trying several blockers and finding none that surfaced this "attempt count" data. Figured others might find it useful too.
Happy to answer questions about implementation or the API if anyone's curious!
